lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A simulation gives you numbers. How do you turn them into a film you can show at a talk?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's MistubaVideo, a set of tools from the ETSim project built on Mitsuba 3, a path tracer.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sequences of 3D models, or recorded body poses and surface wear fields from a simulation. The tools render each frame and encode an MP4 or GIF with FFmpeg.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Because you can change the camera or the lighting without running the simulation again. You can pick front, top or perspective views, denoise on the GPU, and make heatmaps with a surface atlas panel.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Any project can write a versioned manifest file, and the tool validates it. There's even a demo command that makes a synthetic example. The written page has the walkthrough.
